entities.evidence: Noah names Yahweh as the one he blesses.
The title “the God of Shem” identifies Yahweh, named immediately before it.
Noah refers to his son Shem in the phrase “the God of Shem.”
Noah continues speaking of Ham’s son Canaan, whom he cursed in the preceding verse.

analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In בָּרוּךְ יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהֵי שֵׁם, Noah declares Yahweh, the God of Shem, blessed. The participle precedes its subject, יַהְוֶה, and agrees with it in gender and number.
analysis.morphology: Qal passive participle, masculine singular absolute, used predicatively.
analysis.sense: to pronounce Yahweh blessed in praise

analysis.morphology: Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In בָּרוּךְ יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהֵי שֵׁם, the phrase אֱלֹהֵי שֵׁם identifies Yahweh as the God of Shem.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural in form, in the construct state before שֵׁם. Its referent is singular.

analysis.evidence: In יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהֵי שֵׁם, “YHWH, the God of Shem,” the construct form אֱלֹהֵי introduces Shem as the person whose God YHWH is. The following clause names Canaan as a servant.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כְנַעַן is the subject and עֶבֶד is the predicate. The speaker wishes Canaan the status of a servant, and לָמוֹ identifies whom he is to serve.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וִ־ joins the preceding blessing to a wish. The shortened Qal jussive יְהִי is third-person masculine singular, agreeing with כְנַעַן.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: In וִיהִי כְנַעַן עֶבֶד לָמוֹ, “may Canaan be a servant to them,” Canaan is the subject and עֶבֶד describes his role. Noah’s words refer to Ham’s son.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וִיהִי כְנַעַן עֶבֶד לָמוֹ, “may Canaan be a slave to them,” עֶבֶד names the status wished upon Canaan. The following לָמוֹ identifies whom he is to serve.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וִיהִי כְנַעַן עֶבֶד לָמוֹ, “may Canaan be a servant to them,” כְנַעַן is the subject and עֶבֶד names his role. The suffix on לָמוֹ supplies the plural complement of the preposition.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לָ־ takes the poetic third-person masculine plural pronominal suffix ־מוֹ.
analysis.sense: Marks those whom Canaan is to serve.
